senses.gloss: (b. h.) to capture, carry off.—Part. pass. שָׁבוּי; f. שְׁבוּיָה; pl. שְׁבוּיִים, שְׁבוּיִם, שְׁבוּיִין; שְׁבוּיוֹת.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 1:2">Keth. I, 2</cite> <he>הגיורת והש׳ וכ׳</he> a proselyte, a captive, and a slave, converted, redeemed, or freed at an age of less than three years and one day.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 8a:18">B. Bath. 8ᵃ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Chullin 7a:10">Ḥull. 7ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>פדיון ש׳</he>, v. <cite ref="Q00121"><he>פִּדְיוֹן</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 2:5">Shek. II, 5</cite> <he>מותר שבויים לש׳</he> what is left over from a fund collected for the ransom of captives, must be reserved for the ransom of other captives; <he>מותר שבוי לאותו ש׳</he> what is left over from a collection for a certain captive, belongs to that captive. Y. ib. II, 47ᵃ top <he>אין פודין ש׳ בש׳</he> you dare not redeem a captive by surrendering another captive.
<cite ref="Ketubot 51b:17">Keth. 51ᵇ</cite> <he>בש׳ הקלו</he> with regard to a woman redeemed from captivity the practice is more lenient (allowing her husband to live with her again).
<cite ref="Ketubot 51b:17">Ib.</cite> <he>שְׁבוּיֵי מלכות הרי הן כש׳</he> women forced by (Roman) officials come under the law of redeemed captives (are permitted to live with their husbands).
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 4:6">Gitt. IV, 6</cite>, v. <cite ref="Q00110"><he>פָּדָה</he></cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 39a:8">B. Mets. 39ᵃ</cite> <he>שבוי שנ׳ מורידין וכ׳</he> if a person has been captured (banished), we appoint a relative to manage his property.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 104a:16">Snh. 104ᵃ</cite> <he>שני בני אדם שנִשְׁבּוּ וכ׳</he> two persons were captured on Mount Carmel.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 1:57">Lam. R. to I, 16</cite> <he>מעשה במרים … שנִשְׁבֵּית וכ׳</he> it came to pass that Miriam … was carried off (by the Romans), herself and her seven sons.

<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 2:5">Keth. II, 5</cite> <he>נִשְׁבֵּתִי וטהורה אני</he> I was a captive (among gentiles), but I remained pure; <cite ref="Ketubot 23a:13">ib. 23ᵃ</cite> <he>נִשְׁבֵּיתִי</he>; a. fr.
